run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-100a had issues on November 20, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: The app-100a 'payment-api' workload did fail around 13:45–14:45 UTC on 2026-11-20, and its own Loki log lines show why at the application layer: it could not get database connections. A query for ERROR lines in namespace app-100a over 2026-11-20T03:52:30Z–13:50:00Z returned exactly one line, at 13:49:24Z, and from then until the last observed ERROR at 14:44:44Z the pod logged repeated 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' (pool_size 20, active_connections 20, waiting_requests 7–46, wait_time_ms 5,216–26,798), 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use' with error_code DB_CONN_001, and '/healthz' health checks returning status_code 503 described as 'database unreachable' (response_time_ms 5,009–9,684). Before this, that day's logs show healthy behaviour: six DB queries of 15–88 ms between 12:30:17Z and 13:34:45Z and payment processing times of 226–468 ms. One DB query inside the incident window took 1,252 ms versus that baseline. By 2026-11-21T03:07–03:48Z the sampled lines are normal again (queries 16–78 ms, successful payments), and no ERROR line appears after 14:44:44Z in the 14:30Z–03:52Z sample. The evidence therefore describes a roughly one-hour degradation of the payment-api pod caused at the dependency layer by a slow/unreachable database exhausting its fixed 20-connection pool; the database itself is not represented in the cluster (no DB Service among the 30 cluster services, app-100a has only the loki Service) and produced no logs in Loki, where only job=payment-api/namespace=app-100a exists (278 lines in 14 h). Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable in this Run (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every metric and trace call), so no error-rate, latency, restart or trace series could be checked, and the pod's own container stdout could not be read at all (fetch_pod_logs returned no_data). Hence the application-level failure is supported, but the faulting object cannot be named: root cause is null.

claims.text: The first error in namespace app-100a was at 2026-11-20T13:49:24Z: payment-api logged 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' with pool_size 20, active_connections 20, waiting_requests 27, wait_time_ms 17653. A Loki query for ERROR lines over 2026-11-20T03:52:30Z–13:50:00Z returned exactly that one line, so no earlier ERROR line was in that query's result.

payment-api's error lines state 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use' with error_code DB_CONN_001 and stack_trace 'at PaymentService.processPayment()\n at DatabasePool.acquire()', with pool_size 20 and active_connections 20 and waiting_requests rising from 27 to 46 and wait_time_ms from 5,216 to 26,798 between 13:49:24Z and 14:43:57Z.

payment-api logged '/healthz' health-check failures: 'Health check failed - database unreachable', endpoint /healthz, status_code 503, response_time_ms 5009 at 2026-11-20T13:57:29Z and 9684 at 14:01:50Z, plus 6354 at 14:44:44Z.

Before the failure the same pod's own logs show normal database behaviour: 'Database query executed' durations of 15, 18, 30, 61, 65 and 88 ms between 2026-11-20T12:30:17Z and 13:34:45Z, and 'Payment processed successfully' with processing_time_ms 226, 273, 326, 385 and 468 ms.
Inside the incident window one DB query still completed, at 2026-11-20T13:50:55Z with duration_ms 1252 and rows_returned 98, against the 15–88 ms range measured before 13:34:45Z that day.

The latest ERROR line in a query over 2026-11-20T14:30:00Z–2026-11-21T03:52:00Z is timestamped 2026-11-20T14:44:44Z (7 lines returned, all between 14:30:57Z and 14:44:44Z), so the observed error window ends about 55 minutes after it began at 13:49:24Z.

In the sampled hour 2026-11-21T03:00:00Z–03:51:00Z the same pod logged only DEBUG/INFO lines (database queries 16, 17, 44, 45, 64 and 78 ms; 'Payment processed successfully' 157 and 385 ms) with no ERROR line among the 15 lines returned.

Loki holds only one log stream for this workload: a count_over_time grouped query over 2026-11-20T13:52:00Z–2026-11-21T03:52:00Z returned a single series job=payment-api, namespace=app-100a with 278 lines, and a 2026-11-20T13:30:00Z–13:50:00Z grouped query likewise returned only job=payment-api/namespace=app-100a. No database component logs exist in Loki for this window.

Namespace app-100a contains exactly one Service, 'loki' (ClusterIP, port 3100, selector app=loki), and the cluster-wide Service list (30 Services) contains no database Service; nothing in the cluster exposes the database that payment-api reported as unreachable.

Deployment payment-api-100a runs image python:3.9-slim with command python /app/app-direct-push.py, container port 8080, a livenessProbe httpGet /healthz:8080 (initialDelaySeconds 30, periodSeconds 10, timeoutSeconds 10, failureThreshold 3), memory limit 256Mi, and the application files mounted from a Secret volume; it reports 1/1 ready and available.

The cluster objects are post-incident state: pod payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-flds7 was created 2026-11-21T03:51:30Z with restartCount 0 and Ready True, and the only events in the window are 2026-11-21T03:51-era Deployment ScalingReplicaSet (x2), ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate (x2), Pod Scheduled/Created/Pulled/Started (x2 each); otel-demo pods date from 2026-11-20T16:32 and the node's system pods from 16:31. These objects cannot show what existed at 13:45 on 2026-11-20.

The most likely explanation is that the database dependency became slow or unreachable around 13:45–13:49Z, so every one of payment-api's 20 pooled connections stayed busy and new requests waited up to 26.8 s; the app's own health-check message 'database unreachable' and the 1,252 ms query (vs 15–88 ms baseline) point to the dependency rather than to a logic error in the pod.

A second candidate is that request concurrency exceeded the fixed pool capacity (pool_size 20 with waiting_requests 7–46), which would exhaust the pool even with a healthy database; request-rate and concurrency series (app_payment_transactions_total, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count) could not be read because Prometheus returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so this remains unverified.

A third candidate is that the failing /healthz probes (503 after 5,009–9,684 ms, against timeoutSeconds 10 and failureThreshold 3) caused container restarts during the incident; this cannot be confirmed because restart history and kube-state-metrics series were unreadable and the surviving pod (restartCount 0) was created after the incident window.

The degradation was not a total outage of the workload: during the error window the pod still logged a successful 'Database query executed' (1252 ms, 98 rows) at 13:50:55Z, and no ERROR line appears at all in the 2026-11-21T03:07–03:48Z sample, so pool exhaustion was intermittent and had cleared by the next day's samples.

Re-run the metrics side once Prometheus is reachable: rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=...}), app_payment_transactions_total, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total for the deployment's pod over 2026-11-20T13:30–15:00Z, to size the failure rate and settle whether the container restarted.

Ask the database owner for that dependency's own logs and metrics for 2026-11-20T13:40–14:50Z, and review the Secret-mounted /app application configuration to confirm the DB endpoint and the 20-connection pool setting; neither is observable from this Run's sources.

gaps: The pod's own container stdout is unobserved: fetch_pod_logs for payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-flds7 returned status no_data with 0 lines for the current instance and reported no previous instance (HTTP 400 previous terminated container not found), so the workload's operational record rests on its Loki-pushed lines and lines outside the sampled windows are unknown.

Prometheus was unreachable for the whole Run: get_metric_names, get_label_values, get_series, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so app_payment_transactions_total, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, traces_span_metrics_calls_total and kube-state-metrics series (restarts, status) were never read for 13:45Z.

Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services and traces_search for service 'payment' returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and the service list offered only otel-demo names such as 'payment'; nothing shows whether any trace exists for the app-100a payment-api workload.

The database that payment-api reported as unreachable is not visible: no database workload pod exists in any namespace, no database Service exists among the 30 cluster Services, and Loki returned no DB-side log stream (only job=payment-api/namespace=app-100a), so the dependency-side fault is unverified.

The application's configuration (DB host, pool size, timeouts) is mounted from a Secret volume named in the deployment, and Secrets cannot be read in this Run, so the pool-size value in effect during the incident could not be verified.

Restart and OOM history for the payment-api container during 13:45–14:45Z is unavailable: kube-state-metrics/Prometheus were down and the window's events are all dated 2026-11-21T03:51, i.e. after the incident, while the surviving pod (created 2026-11-21T03:51:30Z, restartCount 0) post-dates the incident and carries no previous container state.

A NetworkPolicy query across all namespaces returned status no_data with 0 items, so it is unknown whether any policy existed in app-100a during the incident; among policies, services, endpoints and quotas, only Services and ConfigMaps were actually readable.

No impact on other services could be checked: Loki holds only payment-api lines, and Prometheus/Jaeger were down, so the otel-demo services (including the distinct 'payment' service in namespace otel-demo) were neither shown affected nor shown healthy.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment, configuration or infrastructure change can be correlated with the 13:45Z onset.
next_steps: Restore or re-scope Prometheus access and pull app_payment_transactions_total, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total for 2026-11-20T13:30–15:00Z.
Have the database team check that dependency's availability, connection count and slow-query data for 2026-11-20T13:40–14:50Z.
Review the app-script Secret's DB endpoint and pool settings (pool_size 20, connection timeouts) and consider a bounded increase plus a shorter acquire timeout so waits do not reach 26.8 s.
Confirm whether the 503 /healthz responses (5.0–9.7 s against a 10 s probe timeout) triggered liveness restarts during 13:49–14:45Z.
